root_idea.summary: The root centers on taking up or entering into an action, especially in the construction طَفِقَ يَفْعَلُ كَذَا, “he began doing such-and-such.”
root_idea.development: The core usage is “begin or set about doing,” with continuation possible in context but not lexically required. Classical extensions include remaining attached to a place and attaining a desired object, alongside a causative Form IV usage meaning to cause attainment.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed as the normalized Form I dictionary citation form طَفِقَ.

senses.definition: To begin, set about, or take to doing something.
senses.usage_conditions: Used affirmatively, not with ما. It is ordinarily followed by a non-past verb or verbal predicate; Quranic usage may also present the action as a verbal noun. Continuation may be intended by context but is not required by the verb itself.

other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the construction طَفِقَ فُلَانٌ بِمَا أَرَادَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To keep to or cling to a place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with a place in the expression طَفِقَ المَوْضِعَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause someone or something to attain or reach another person or thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form IV, including the construction أَطْفَقَهُ اللهُ بِهِ, “God caused him or it to attain him or it.”

lane_unit_coverage.note: Covers the Form I meaning of beginning or taking up an action and its Quranic construction.
Independent meaning of keeping to a place.

cautions: In Quran 38:33, the action introduced by طَفِقَ is interpreted variously as cutting with a sword or wiping/stroking; the verb itself retains the sense of taking up or beginning that action.
